summary.text: A 23-year-old male had chronic autoimmune uveitis since the age of 13 and a family history of MS in two uncles and idiopathic epilepsy in his sister. Methotrexate gave a poor response and was substituted by Cyclosporine and Azathioprine, which achieved a better control. A year ago Azathioprine was suspended for a while because of the political situation and Adalimumab was initiated.

Few days following the second dose of Adalimumab he developed right hemibody anesthesia that lasted two weeks and was successfully treated with intravenous methylprednisolone. Adalimumab was then stopped, and Azathioprine at a dose of 3 mg/kg and oral prednisolone were initiated. Eight months following Adalimumab infusion he had right lower limb paresis, also successfully treated with methylprednisolone, and normal strength was restored within three weeks.

Five months later brain MRI revealed multiple periventricular and juxtacortical lesions and a T2 hypersignal lesion in the spinal cord at the level of C4, none contrast enhancing. Visually evoked potentials and CSF analysis were normal, CSF was negative for oligoclonal bands, ANA, RF and ANCA were negative and HLA analysis revealed HLA-B27. Examination showed anisocoria, bilaterally sluggish reaction to light, mild right facial and body hemihypoesthesia, generalized hyperreflexia (+3) and mild right lower limb spasticity. Diagnosis of Adalimumab induced MS was suspected.

Brain MRI with contrast was repeated and revealed no new lesions comparing with the previous one. The patient was referred by a rheumatologist to a neurology clinic for consultation and followup, and there has been no new attack since then. The treatment plan was continued with no modification and regular clinical and radiological followup was suggested; Rituximab would be the treatment of choice if hints of clinical or radiological activity are noticed later on.
